Respondents  Through  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIBHU BAKHRU  ORDER % 22.01.2019 1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
W.P.(C) 645/2019 & CM No.2944/2019 2.

Although, the present petition is styled as a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, it is required to be treated as an appeal under Section 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The scope of the present proceedings, therefore, extends to both the question of law as well as of fact.
3. The petitioners claims that the penalty have been imposed on the petitioners on the premise that the petitioners are repeat offender.
It is the petitioner's case that they cannot be treated as a repeat offender as the petitioners have not committed any offence twice.
The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners states that misbranding is a generic term and includes several offences.
The petitioners have been found guilty of not putting the correct facts on the label of the product and were, accordingly, punished.

The petitioners have now been found guilty of the relevant regulations and as much as the size of the label does not conform to the requisite size, but there is no allegation that the contents of the label are incorrect or deceptive.
4. The learned counsel further submits that the said offence also cannot be termed as an offence of misbranding under the provisions of Section 3(1)(zf) of the said Act.
